A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ZeroTuning, with matching authors, core methodology, benchmarks, and Appendices A–P. Text, equations, tables, and figures are accessible and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, multiple-choice QA, and MT-Bench results, together with layer/head ablations, robustness experiments, and error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a controlled BoolQ fine-tuning comparison and population-level analysis in Appendix E.1.

M1.justification: Head profiling, selective initial-token scaling, renormalization, and supervised accuracy-based or unsupervised entropy-based calibration remain unchanged. Section 3.6 expands the description of possible unlabeled calibration sources; applying ZeroTuning after LoRA uses the existing procedure.

E1.justification: The same 15 datasets and classification, multiple-choice QA, and conversation tasks remain. The added fine-tuning study uses BoolQ, and the population analysis uses SST-2. Existing context, prompt, few-shot, decoding, and quantization scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Section 6.2 adds LoRA SFT as an evaluated comparator and includes SFT followed by ZeroTuning. Vanilla, ACT, Auto-PASTA, and the MT-Bench comparator set remain unchanged in their corresponding comparisons. Section 5 also newly reports a temperature-tuning comparison, without specifying settings or scores.

E3.justification: The new BoolQ comparison controls labeled-data availability at 500 examples and uses LoRA rank 4 for three epochs. Figure 15 adds an analysis of 872 SST-2 samples, divided into 438 uncertain and 434 certain samples. These are added evaluation settings; existing benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 extends individual error cases with population-level probability and accuracy trajectories, examining whether aggregation stabilizes the calibration signal. Section 6.2 adds a test of ZeroTuning’s compatibility with SFT. The extensive existing ablations and robustness analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose seed 42 for calibration-sample selection and provide no repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new population-confidence plots do not change statistical uncertainty reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes unsupervised LogiQA accuracy from 43.50 to 43.40, retaining the 67.02 average although the revised entries average 67.00. Section 6.2 adds BoolQ scores of 81.20 for LoRA and 83.60 for LoRA plus ZeroTuning, alongside 69.60 vanilla and 82.40 ZeroTuning. Figure 15 adds aggregate trends, and Section 5 reports no improvement from temperature tuning. Other benchmark tables retain their values.

T1.justification: Equations 1–19, Proposition 1 and its proof in Appendix C, and the attention-versus-key-scaling derivations in Appendix G remain mathematically unchanged. Section 3.1 edits explanatory prose without revising the formal analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim of monotonically controlling downstream attention entropy with the narrower claim of systematically reshaping attention patterns. The conclusion changes general superiority over previous methods to being competitive with, and often stronger than, prior baselines. The central contribution and headline performance claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix E.1 adds cancellation and reinforcement explanations for why population averaging avoids individual calibration traps. Section 6.2 develops the interpretation of ZeroTuning as complementary to SFT, explicitly limiting its comparison to a small LoRA setup and acknowledging potentially stronger fine-tuning configurations. Existing failure boundaries remain.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 newly reports approximately 4–5 minutes for Llama-3.1-8B calibration on one unspecified GPU. Section 6.2 documents the LoRA data budget, rank, and epochs. Section 3.6 clarifies held-out unlabeled-corpus and test-batch calibration options. Existing implementation details, prompts, and code/demo access information remain.

R1.justification: The reference list adds Beyond Detection and Latex2Layout and removes Li et al.’s The Choice of Divergence. Existing Han papers receive publication-metadata updates. Section 6.2 develops positioning relative to SFT, while the central relationship to attention-steering and attention-sink research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, several Section 3 explanations, and conclusion. The numbered introductory findings become a compact roadmap and boxed Insights summary, and a Further Discussion section is inserted before the conclusion. Headers change to ICLR 2026 publication wording. An introductory citation becomes an unresolved question mark.

P2.justification: v3 removes the attention illustration in v2 Figure 3, adds the population plot as Figure 15 and an unnumbered BoolQ SFT table, and introduces the Insights box. Existing empirical plots are retained with relocation or renumbering. Tables and prompt boxes are reflowed within the same overall visual design.

improvement.justification: v3 better aligns its abstract with the unchanged formal analysis, supplies initial controlled evidence for SFT complementarity previously suggested as future work, and extends individual error cases with population evidence. Calibration-cost disclosure improves practical clarity. These are limited gains: the SFT comparison covers one small setup without reported uncertainty, the temperature comparison lacks details, and v3 introduces an inconsistent Table 4 average and an unresolved citation.
